sections.html:
Baldwin County sits on the Gulf coast on the eastern side of Mobile Bay. Bay Minette is the county seat and Daphne is the largest city. The population was 231,767 in the 2020 census, up from 182,265 in 2010, and the 2025 estimate is 267,761. Of the 124,148 housing units counted in 2020, 25.0 percent were vacant.

Growth is uneven. The Foley subdivision went from 48,089 to 64,862 people between 2010 and 2020, and the Daphne subdivision, which includes Spanish Fort, went from 41,295 to 55,767. The Stockton area stayed nearly flat, at 3,804 and 3,745. Two houses in the same county can sit in very different markets, so look at numbers for your own part of the county and not the county average.

School zoning varies too. The county has three public school districts: Baldwin County, Gulf Shores City and Orange Beach City, the last formed in 2022. A house in Orange Beach and one in Bay Minette share a county but not a school system, and buyers ask about that.

sections.h2: Cities and towns in the county
sections.html:
Baldwin has nine cities and five towns. The cities are Bay Minette, Daphne, Fairhope, Foley, Gulf Shores, Loxley, Orange Beach, Robertsdale and Spanish Fort. The towns are Elberta, Magnolia Springs, Perdido Beach, Silverhill and Summerdale. Point Clear, Fort Morgan, Bon Secour, Lillian, Stapleton and Stockton are unincorporated or census designated places.

Your tax bill shows which levies apply to your address, so read it before you set a price or talk to a buyer. For census purposes the Foley subdivision takes in Gulf Shores, Magnolia Springs and most of Orange Beach, the Daphne subdivision includes Spanish Fort, the Robertsdale subdivision includes Loxley and Silverhill, and the Elberta subdivision includes Perdido Beach.

Tropical weather is a regular fact of life here, and the county has been declared a disaster area several times, with Frederic in September 1979, Ivan in September 2004 and Sally in September 2020 among the named storms. Buyers on the coast look hard at roof condition, wind and flood coverage, drainage and any storm repair left half done.

A house with an open insurance claim or unrepaired damage is a harder sale than a tidy one. If your house is near water, keep your survey and any flood certificate handy. Some owners choose a cash sale to skip repair loans, condition-based appraisals and buyers who walk away after an inspection. We purchase houses as they stand, storm-damaged ones included.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Baldwin has an elected revenue commissioner who serves the whole county. The Collections Division collects tax on all real and personal property assessed in the county. Taxes are due October 1 each year, and courtesy notices usually go out before then so owners can check their mailing address. Collections can be reached at 251-937-0245.

DateWhat it means
October 1Taxes due
December 31Last day before taxes are delinquent
February 28Last day for personal and business checks

After December 31 penalties and interest begin to accrue, and the owner has to contact Collections for the new amount due. Personal and business checks are accepted between October 1 and February 28.

If your mortgage company pays through escrow, confirming the payment is still your job. The county offers an EscrowCheck tool that shows the real-time status of escrow payments from banks and lenders. Search with the parcel number, entered without dashes.

If you cannot find your bill, call the Collections Division before October 1 and ask for a copy. Missing mail does not change the due date, and a late payment adds penalties and interest. Keep proof of payment, such as the receipt or the EscrowCheck result, in the same folder as your closing papers so the title company can see the taxes are current.

The Revenue Commission posts instructions on how to protest an appraised value, whether a protest can be filed by phone, what happens if you miss your hearing and what to do if you never received a valuation notice. A fillable online protest form is available. Answers are collapsed on the county's FAQ page, so open each question for the current instructions.

Do not confuse the valuation notice with your tax bill. The notice states the appraised value and starts the protest clock. The bill arrives later for the October 1 due date.

If you plan to sell, do not let a protest sit. A buyer's title company wants the tax record current, and a pending protest can leave the amount unsettled at closing.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the lien auction
sections.html:
Alabama's 2018 legislature passed Act 2018-577, which gave counties an alternative to selling the property itself: selling the tax lien. Baldwin moved to lien sales in 2019, beginning with tax year 2018 delinquent properties. Every lien for unpaid and delinquent real property taxes is subject to public auction, and the sale runs on the GovEase platform.

The county's tax lien auction page answers the questions an owner would ask: whether ownership transfers when a lien is bought, how to redeem a lien, what happens to liens that do not sell and whether training is available for the platform. Read those answers before you decide anything.

State redemption rules still apply. Our Alabama tax sale page summarizes who can redeem and how long they have.

The title company pays the delinquent tax, and any lien redemption amount, from your proceeds at closing. Gather three things first: the parcel number, the tax years owed and a payoff figure from Collections.

If the county sold a lien on your parcel, ask Collections what the payoff includes. Request the figure in writing and give the title company time to confirm it. A stale number is the usual cause of a delayed closing.

  1. Call Collections and ask for the payoff for each tax year owed.
  2. Ask whether a lien was sold and who holds it.
  3. Give the written figure to the title company.
  4. Confirm the payment is recorded after closing.

We buy Baldwin County houses as they are, including ones with delinquent tax, storm damage or deferred repairs, so you do not have to fix anything or clear the balance before you accept an offer.

What a cash sale skips is worth spelling out. There is no listing prep, no buyer loan waiting on an appraisal, and no repair negotiation after an inspection. You still need clear paperwork: bring the most recent tax bill, any notice you received from the Revenue Commission, and your mortgage payoff if you have a loan. The title company handles the deed, the payoff of taxes and liens, and the final numbers, and you see them before you sign.

faqs.q: When are Baldwin County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1 each year. They become delinquent after December 31, and penalties and interest accrue after that date.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Baldwin County?
faqs.a: The Collections Division of the Baldwin County Revenue Commission. You can reach it at 251-937-0245.

faqs.q: What if my mortgage company pays my Baldwin County tax?
faqs.a: Confirm that it did, because that remains the owner's responsibility. The county's EscrowCheck tool shows whether an escrow payment reached the county.

faqs.q: Does Baldwin County sell tax liens or the property itself?
faqs.a: Liens. The county began selling them in 2019 with tax year 2018 delinquents under Act 2018-577, and every lien for unpaid real property taxes goes to public auction.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Baldwin County house with unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes, in many cases. The tax and any lien payoff come out of the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff figure from the Collections Division first.
